category_title: Students with externalizing behavior problems including work refusal and temper tantrums
minimal_context: The student is presenting his weekly diary to the teacher to check for a parent signature required for the reward system.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our weekly check. Please bring your diary to my desk so I can check for your parent's signature.

STUDENT: Yes, but I haven’t had it signed.

TUTOR: Please hand me the diary anyway so I can look at it.

STUDENT: (Hands over the diary, pointing to a note written by his parent) Look, she wrote: 'J handed me this book to sign. I didn’t sign it. He had the initiative and intent.'

TUTOR: I see the note, but without the actual signature, you do not meet the requirement for the weekly reward.

STUDENT: (Throws a temper tantrum, pushing the diary off the desk) That's not fair! I'm not doing any of my work today if I don't get the reward!

options.A: Implement relatively tight timelines for the student to complete the weekly diary requirements and other classroom tasks.
options.B: Provide a clear beginning and end for each classroom task, including the weekly diary check and reward process.
options.C: Implement a healing-lake visualization, encouraging the student to observe the lake carefully and notice that it is always changing, yet always itself.
options.D: Use the weekly diaries effectively as tools of regulative discourse, not only for the student, but also for their parents.
